common_name: Black Knight Canna (Deep Maroon-Red Flowered Bronze Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Plant divided rhizomes once soil has warmed past 60°F; Black Knight carries velvety, deep maroon-red blooms held above purple-bronze foliage for a smoldering color combination distinct from the brighter scarlet cultivars.

directions: Set rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, and feed monthly through the growing season to sustain both the dark foliage color and continuous bloom. Black Knight pairs richly pigmented, near-black flowers with bronzy-purple leaves, giving it a moodier presence than red-flowered green-leaf cultivars and making it a strong anchor in hot-color or tropical-themed borders. Keep the soil consistently moist but well drained, since cannas are heavy feeders and drinkers that rot quickly in standing water. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground and forms an expanding clump; farther north, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost blackens the foliage.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Canna Growing Guide

common_name: Endeavour Canna (Australian Bright Red-Flowered Glossy Green Canna)

planting.note: Divide and plant rhizomes after soil has warmed; Endeavour, an Australian-bred cultivar, produces vivid true-red flowers over glossy, unmarked dark green foliage, a cleaner look than the many bronze- or striped-leaf canna selections.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in fertile, well-amended soil in full sun, watering deeply and feeding regularly during the growing season for the strongest bloom. Endeavour was selected in Australia for its glossy, disease-resistant green foliage and abundant, well-held scarlet-red flowers, traits that have made it a favorite where canna rust and leaf-spot are a concern. It flowers continuously from early summer through frost and combines well with variegated or bronze-leaf cannas as a foliage contrast. In zone 9 and warmer, established clumps overwinter in the ground; elsewhere, lift rhizomes after frost and store them dry.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Tropical Plants for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Lucifer Canna (Dwarf Red Flowers Edged in Yellow)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Lucifer is a dwarf bedding canna bearing red petals rimmed in bright yellow on compact plants with plain green foliage, well suited to the front of a border or large containers.

directions: Set rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, evenly moist soil in full sun, and deadhead spent flower spikes to keep the compact plants blooming through summer. Lucifer's low, tidy stature and distinctive red-and-yellow bicolor blooms make it one of the few cannas suited to mixed bedding schemes and container plantings rather than the back of a tropical border. It is a heavy feeder like other cannas, so a monthly balanced fertilizer supports continuous flowering. In zone 9 and warmer it can stay in the ground year-round; in colder zones, lift and store the rhizomes after frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Panache Canna (Heirloom Apricot-Pink Flowered Blue-Green Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Panache is an heirloom cultivar with narrow, blue-green foliage and soft apricot-pink flowers, a subtler look than the bold striped or bronze-leaf canna hybrids.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun, and stake if needed in windy sites given its tall, narrow habit. Panache carries the slender, glaucous blue-green leaves associated with its Canna glauca parentage along with loose sprays of soft apricot-pink flowers, giving it a more naturalistic look that suits perennial borders and pondside plantings rather than bold tropical display beds. Keep it well watered through summer, since cannas are heavy drinkers, while ensuring drainage is adequate to prevent rhizome rot. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground and slowly expands into a clump; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost.

common_name: Yellow King Humbert Canna (Heirloom Yellow Flowers Speckled Red, Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Yellow King Humbert is an heirloom sport of the classic King Humbert canna, bearing golden-yellow flowers flecked with red over the same bronze-green foliage.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, feeding monthly to support the large flower spikes and bronzy foliage color. Yellow King Humbert arose as a color sport of the old bronze-leaf 'King Humbert' line and pairs the same broad, purple-bronze leaves with golden-yellow blooms speckled in red, offering a warmer color echo for gardeners who already grow the scarlet-flowered Red King Humbert. It is a vigorous, tall heirloom well suited to the back of a border or as a tropical accent. In zone 9 and warmer, clumps overwinter in the ground and expand yearly; in colder zones, lift and store rhizomes after frost.
sources: American Canna Society — Heirloom Canna Registry
Louisiana State University AgCenter — Tropical Plants for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Tropical Bronze Scarlet Canna (AAS-Winning Dwarf Seed-Grown Bronze-Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes or seed-grown transplants once soil has warmed; Tropical Bronze Scarlet was an early All-America Selections seed canna bred for uniform, compact plants with bronze-purple foliage beneath vivid scarlet blooms.

directions: Start seed indoors or plant divided rhizomes once soil has warmed, setting plants in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun. Tropical Bronze Scarlet was among the first seed-grown canna selections to combine reliable first-year flowering with rich bronze-purple foliage, a color trait more typical of rhizome-propagated heirlooms than earlier green-leaf seed strains. Its compact, uniform habit and scarlet blooms make it well suited to bedding schemes where taller heirloom cannas would overwhelm the design. Feed monthly and keep soil evenly moist but well drained, since cannas rot readily in waterlogged ground. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in place; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after frost.
sources: All-America Selections — Tropical Bronze Scarlet Canna Award Notes
American Canna Society — Seed-Grown Canna Breeding
